# Task

The seller's book goes to print Friday and legal want the fair-housing pass signed off
before it does. The section inventory and our compliance standard RE-FH-9 are both in
`input/`. Work from the standard rather than from memory — it was amended this year and the
book has not entirely caught up.

Give me `fairhousing_audit.csv`: two columns, `section_id` and `finding`, one row per
section in inventory order, with a header. `finding` is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`,
`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`, `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` or `none`, and where a section trips more
than one rule join the labels with `|` in that same order. Nothing else in that file
please — the print vendor's importer takes the two columns and chokes on anything more.

Then `fairhousing_memo.md` explaining what you found and why, with enough reasoning that
legal can sign off without re-reading RE-FH-9 themselves.

And `results.json` for the sign-off form. Count sections, not labels:

- `section_count` — sections in the inventory
- `flagged_count` — sections whose `finding` is not `none`
- `personal_narrative_count`, `protected_lang_count`, `disclaimer_missing_count` — sections
  whose `finding` includes that label

---

Save all three into your current working directory, at exactly those filenames. Writing them
is the deliverable; confirm each exists before you answer. Your working directory is
writable and the read-only attachments are in `input/`.

# Fair-housing audit — seller's book (RE-FH-9)

**Prepared for:** Legal sign-off
**Standard applied:** RE-FH-9, *Real-estate marketing collateral fair-housing standard*, including the 2026 amendments at §5.
**Source inventory:** `input/seller_book_sections.csv` (30 sections, audited in inventory order).
**Deliverables:** `fairhousing_audit.csv`, `results.json`, this memo.

## 1. What was applied and how

Each of the 30 sections was assessed against three operative rules. A section may carry
more than one finding, reported in the fixed order `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE | PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE | DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.

- **§1 Personal-narrative solicitation → `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`.** Any section, in
  any role, that solicits or presents a buyer "love letter" or comparable personal narrative
  tied to buyer identity. Applied regardless of role.
- **§2 Protected-class language → `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`.** A section naming a
  protected-class term, or a recognised proxy, trips this rule. Per §3, the only thing that
  can shield disclosure text from §2 is a notice that names **every** required class; an
  abridged notice earns **no** exemption at all, and the exemption, where it applies, covers
  §2 and nothing else. Crucially, protected-class terms a section uses in its **own prose,
  outside the notice, are never covered** — a compliant notice does not launder them.
- **§4 Required disclaimer → `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.** A section in a role responsible for
  carrying the disclosure must carry a compliant (complete) notice; carrying none, or an
  abridged one, is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. Per §4 as drafted the responsible role is
  `closing_page`; per the §5b amendment `agent_bio` is now equally responsible. Sections in
  any other role are **not** assessed under §4.

### The required-class list (used to judge every notice)

Per §2 the protected classes are race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national
origin, disability, sexual orientation and veteran status. The **§5a amendment** adds
**marital status** and **source of income** to the required disclosure. A compliant notice
must therefore name all **eleven** classes. A notice naming even ten of them is *abridged*
for the purposes of §3 and §4, whatever else it contains. I audited against this amended
list, not against the pre-amendment template the book happens to carry (per the §5a
instruction to audit against the amended list until the template is reissued).

### Proxies treated as protected-class language (§2)

- "churches", "parish school", "parish hall", "congregation-centred", "faith community" → religion (houses of worship / parish or faith schools).
- "family-oriented street", "churchgoing households", "young families", "long-established families" → familial status (and, where faith-tinged, religion), i.e. describing a street/neighbourhood by the kind of household that lives on it.
- Bare bedroom counts ("four-bedroom") were treated as property description, **not** as household-type proxies, and did not trigger §2.

## 2. Headline numbers

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Sections in inventory (`section_count`) | 30 |
| Sections flagged, finding ≠ `none` (`flagged_count`) | 19 |
| Sections including `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` | 7 |
| Sections including `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` | 11 |
| Sections including `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` | 8 |

11 sections are clean (`none`): SEC-01, SEC-06, SEC-10, SEC-12, SEC-13, SEC-16, SEC-18, SEC-20, SEC-23, SEC-26, SEC-28.

## 3. Findings by section, with reasoning

### Personal-narrative solicitation (§1) — 7 sections

These sections ask the buyer for a personal letter/note tied to identity, which is the
"love letter" risk RE-FH-9 §1 prohibits:

- **SEC-02** (`seller_letter`): "write us a letter about what brought you here and what this home would mean to you."
- **SEC-07** (`closing_page`): "Send a personal note about yourself along with the offer; the one that moves us most is the one we will take."
- **SEC-08** (`disclosure_block`): "We invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves and why this home suits them."
- **SEC-17** (`seller_letter`): "Include a covering letter introducing yourself — the sellers would like to know who is buying."
- **SEC-24** (`closing_page`): "write us a letter about what brought you here and what this home would mean to you."
- **SEC-27** (`seller_letter`): "Send a personal note about yourself along with the offer; the one that moves us most is the one we will take."
- **SEC-29** (`agent_bio`): "We invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves and why this home suits them."

Note SEC-08 and SEC-29 each carry a **complete** notice yet still fail §1 — the §3 exemption
is narrow and shields only §2; §1 applies to every section regardless of role or notice.

### Protected-class language (§2) — 11 sections

Two distinct mechanisms produced these:

**(a) Protected-class terms in the section's own prose** (never covered by any exemption):

- **SEC-03** (`listing_copy`): "family-oriented street … two churches … parish school."
- **SEC-07** (`closing_page`): "churchgoing households … long-established families."
- **SEC-09** (`agent_bio`): "young families … parish hall … toddler group."
- **SEC-17** (`seller_letter`): "congregation-centred neighbourhood … same faith community."
- **SEC-19** (`closing_page`): same neighbourhood text as SEC-03, *and* it carries a complete notice.
- **SEC-25** (`listing_copy`): "churchgoing households … long-established families."

**(b) An abridged notice that loses the §3 exemption**, so the notice's own class-terms count:

- **SEC-04** (`disclosure_block`): notice names 9 classes — omits marital status and source of income (§5a).
- **SEC-11** (`closing_page`): same 9-class abridgement.
- **SEC-14** (`agent_bio`): same 9-class abridgement.
- **SEC-15** (`closing_page`): notice names only race, color, religion, sex (4 classes).
- **SEC-22** (`disclosure_block`): notice names 6 classes (race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin).

### Required disclaimer (§4) — 8 sections

Responsible roles are `closing_page` and (per §5b) `agent_bio`. A responsible section with
no notice, or an abridged one, is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`:

- **No notice at all:** SEC-05 (`closing_page`), SEC-21 (`agent_bio`), SEC-30 (`closing_page`).
- **Abridged notice** (missing marital status and/or source of income, or other classes):
  SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15.

### Sections hitting more than one rule

- **SEC-07** — all three: `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE|PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE|DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.
- **SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-14, SEC-15** — `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE|DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.
- **SEC-17** — `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE|PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`.

## 4. Two cases legal should look at closely (counter-intuitive but correct under RE-FH-9)

1. **Disclosure-block sections with abridged notices are flagged for language, not for a
   missing disclaimer.** SEC-04 and SEC-22 are `disclosure_block` sections whose notices are
   abridged. They earn `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` because the abridged notice forfeits the §3
   exemption (so its own class-terms count under §2). They do **not** earn
   `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`, because §4's responsible-role list is `closing_page` and `agent_bio`
   only — `disclosure_block` is not assessed under §4. This is deliberate under the standard
   as written; if the intent was to hold disclosure blocks to §4 as well, that is a
   standard-amendment question, not an audit call.

2. **A compliant notice does not cure protected-class language written in the section's own
   prose.** SEC-19 (`closing_page`) carries a fully compliant eleven-class notice, yet is
   still `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` because its property-description prose ("family-oriented
   street … two churches … parish school") names protected-class proxies outside the
   notice. §3 is explicit that own-prose terms are never covered. The same principle is why
   SEC-08 and SEC-29 are `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` despite complete notices — the §3
   exemption shields only §2.

## 5. Bottom line for sign-off

19 of 30 sections carry at least one finding. The book cannot go to print as-is. The
recurring, fixable patterns are: (i) buyer "love letter" solicitations still present in
seven sections; (ii) neighbourhood/agent copy still describing streets and households by
religion and family type; and (iii) notices still using the pre-§5a template that omits
**marital status** and **source of income** — which both abridges the disclosure (triggering
§4 on `closing_page`/`agent_bio` sections) and, on `disclosure_block` sections, forfeits the
§2 exemption so the notice's own language becomes a violation. Reissuing the disclosure
template to the eleven-class list would clear several `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` and
`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` findings at once, but would not touch the §1 personal-narrative
solicitations or the §2 own-prose proxy language, which require copy edits.

steps.message:
All three deliverables exist and are validated in `/app`:

- **`fairhousing_audit.csv`** — 2 columns (`section_id,finding`), header + 30 rows in inventory order, valid labels only.
- **`fairhousing_memo.md`** — full reasoning for legal, citing RE-FH-9 §1–§5.
- **`results.json`** — `section_count: 30, flagged_count: 19, personal_narrative_count: 7, protected_lang_count: 11, disclaimer_missing_count: 8`.

Key audit calls worth legal's attention:
- **§5a drove most of the flags.** The standing notice template omits **marital status** and **source of income**, so it's *abridged* under the amended 11-class list. That abridgement makes `closing_page`/`agent_bio` sections `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` and, on `disclosure_block` sections, forfeits the §3 exemption so the notice's own wording becomes `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` (SEC-04, SEC-22).
- **§5b brought `agent_bio` into §4** — SEC-09, SEC-14, SEC-21 now fail disclaimer where they previously escaped.
- **A complete notice doesn't cure own-prose language or love-letter asks.** SEC-19 is `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` despite a compliant notice (its property copy names "churches/parish school/family-oriented street"); SEC-08 and SEC-29 are `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` despite complete notices — §3 exempts only §2.
- **`disclosure_block` is not a §4 responsible role**, so abridged-notice disclosure blocks get `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` but *not* `DISCLAIMER_MISSING` (SEC-04, SEC-22) — correct under the standard as written, flagged in the memo in case counsel wants the standard itself amended.

Net: **19 of 30 sections flagged; the book is not print-ready as-is.** Reissuing the disclosure template to the 11-class list would clear several findings at once, but the §1 love-letter solicitations and §2 own-prose proxy language require copy edits.
